name: Hypertension
summary: Persistently raised arterial blood pressure (clinic readings of 140/90 mmHg or higher, confirmed by ambulatory or home monitoring) that increases the risk of stroke, heart, and kidney disease.
treatment: Lifestyle measures (salt reduction, weight loss, exercise, limiting alcohol, stopping smoking) plus antihypertensives stepped up to target: ACE inhibitor or ARB, calcium channel blocker, and/or thiazide-like diuretic. Bloods and urine for target-organ damage at diagnosis, then blood pressure review every few weeks while titrating and at least yearly once controlled.

name: Hyperlipidemia
summary: Raised blood levels of LDL cholesterol and/or triglycerides that accelerate atherosclerosis and raise cardiovascular risk, usually without symptoms.
treatment: Cardiovascular risk assessment and lifestyle changes (diet low in saturated fat, exercise, weight loss, stopping smoking), with a statin as first-line drug therapy when risk warrants; ezetimibe or PCSK9-targeted therapy is added if targets are not met. Lipid profile and liver tests are repeated about 3 months after starting, then annually.

name: Osteoarthritis
summary: Degenerative joint disease with cartilage loss and bony change, most often in the knees, hips, and hands, causing pain on use, brief morning stiffness, and reduced function.
treatment: Education, weight loss, and structured exercise or physiotherapy as core treatment, with topical NSAIDs, then oral NSAIDs at the lowest effective dose with gastroprotection, and occasional intra-articular corticosteroid injections for flares. Joint replacement is considered when pain and disability persist despite these measures.

name: Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease
summary: Recurrent reflux of stomach contents into the oesophagus causing heartburn and regurgitation at least weekly, sometimes with oesophagitis.
treatment: Lifestyle changes (weight loss, smaller meals, avoiding late meals and trigger foods, raising the head of the bed, stopping smoking) plus an 8-week course of a proton pump inhibitor, then stepping down to the lowest effective dose or on-demand use. Endoscopy if there are alarm features (difficulty swallowing, weight loss, bleeding, anaemia) or age over about 55 with new symptoms.

name: Type 2 diabetes mellitus
summary: Chronic hyperglycaemia from insulin resistance and progressive beta-cell failure, diagnosed by HbA1c of 48 mmol/mol (6.5%) or higher, with risk of cardiovascular, kidney, eye, and nerve complications.
treatment: Structured education, diet, weight management, and exercise, with metformin first line and an SGLT2 inhibitor or GLP-1 receptor agonist added for cardiovascular or kidney risk or poor control, and insulin when needed. HbA1c every 3 to 6 months, plus annual eye screening, foot checks, kidney function, and blood pressure and lipid management.

name: Chronic low back pain
summary: Non-specific pain in the lumbar region lasting more than 12 weeks, without a serious underlying cause, often with fluctuating flares and impact on work and sleep.
treatment: Screening for red flags, reassurance, and staying active, with structured exercise, physiotherapy, and psychological approaches such as CBT; NSAIDs short-term for flares, avoiding long-term opioids. Imaging only for red flags or before a specialist procedure, and referral to a pain clinic or spinal service for persistent disabling pain or radicular symptoms.

name: Chronic kidney disease (stages 3-4)
summary: Reduced kidney function (eGFR below 60 mL/min/1.73m2) and/or kidney damage such as albuminuria persisting for more than 3 months, often due to diabetes or hypertension.
treatment: Blood pressure control with an ACE inhibitor or ARB, an SGLT2 inhibitor where indicated, statin therapy, and glucose control in diabetes, avoiding nephrotoxic drugs such as NSAIDs. Regular monitoring of eGFR, albumin-to-creatinine ratio, potassium, and anaemia and bone markers, with nephrology review and planning for kidney replacement therapy if function keeps declining.

name: Asthma
summary: Chronic inflammatory airway disease with variable, reversible airflow obstruction causing episodic wheeze, breathlessness, chest tightness, and cough, with periodic exacerbations.
treatment: Inhaled corticosteroid-containing maintenance therapy (often an ICS-formoterol combination as maintenance and reliever), stepped up with long-acting bronchodilators or biologics if uncontrolled, plus inhaler technique checks, trigger avoidance, and a written action plan. Exacerbations are treated with inhaled bronchodilators and a short course of oral corticosteroids, with review within days.

name: Major depressive disorder
summary: A mood disorder with at least two weeks of persistently low mood or loss of interest plus symptoms such as sleep and appetite change, fatigue, poor concentration, guilt, and thoughts of death, often recurring.
treatment: Risk assessment including suicidality, then psychological therapy (CBT, behavioural activation, interpersonal therapy) and/or an antidepressant, usually an SSRI first line, with review within 2 to 4 weeks of starting. Antidepressants are continued for at least 6 months after remission, longer for recurrent episodes, with urgent referral to mental health services for high risk or psychotic features.
duration: months to years, often recurring, with periodic review

name: Coronary artery disease (stable angina)
summary: Atherosclerotic narrowing of the coronary arteries causing exertional chest pain relieved by rest or nitrates, with a risk of acute coronary syndrome.
treatment: Antiplatelet therapy (aspirin), high-intensity statin, sublingual nitrate for attacks, and anti-anginal therapy with a beta-blocker or calcium channel blocker, plus risk-factor control and cardiac rehabilitation. CT coronary angiography or functional testing confirms the diagnosis, with invasive angiography and PCI or bypass surgery if symptoms persist on medical therapy or anatomy is high risk.

name: Hypothyroidism
summary: Underactive thyroid, most often autoimmune (Hashimoto thyroiditis), with raised TSH and low free T4 causing fatigue, weight gain, cold intolerance, constipation, and dry skin.
treatment: Levothyroxine replacement, started at a dose adjusted for age and cardiac disease and titrated against TSH measured 6 to 8 weeks after each change. Once stable, TSH is checked annually and treatment is continued for life.

name: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
summary: Progressive, largely irreversible airflow limitation from chronic bronchitis and emphysema, usually caused by smoking, with chronic cough, sputum, breathlessness, and exacerbations.
treatment: Smoking cessation, vaccinations, and pulmonary rehabilitation, with inhaled long-acting bronchodilators (LAMA and LABA), adding an inhaled corticosteroid for frequent exacerbations with raised eosinophils, and long-term oxygen for chronic hypoxaemia. Exacerbations are treated with short-acting bronchodilators, a short course of oral corticosteroids, and antibiotics if sputum is purulent, with follow-up within weeks.

name: Generalized anxiety disorder
summary: Excessive, hard-to-control worry about many areas of life on most days for at least six months, with restlessness, tension, poor sleep, irritability, and physical symptoms.
treatment: Stepped care: education and guided self-help, then high-intensity CBT or applied relaxation, and/or an SSRI (or SNRI) first line, avoiding long-term benzodiazepines. Review 2 to 4 weeks after starting medication and continue for at least a year if effective.
duration: months to years, with periodic review

name: Atrial fibrillation
summary: An irregularly irregular atrial arrhythmia causing palpitations, breathlessness, or fatigue, and a major risk factor for cardioembolic stroke.
treatment: Stroke risk assessment (CHA2DS2-VASc) with a direct oral anticoagulant when indicated, rate control with a beta-blocker or rate-limiting calcium channel blocker, and rhythm control by cardioversion, antiarrhythmic drugs, or catheter ablation for selected patients. Treatment of triggers and comorbidities (hypertension, thyroid disease, alcohol, sleep apnoea) and regular review of rate, bleeding risk, and kidney function.

name: Heart failure
summary: A clinical syndrome in which structural or functional heart disease impairs filling or ejection, causing breathlessness, fatigue, and fluid retention, with raised natriuretic peptides.
treatment: Loop diuretics for congestion, and for reduced ejection fraction the four pillars titrated to tolerated doses: ACE inhibitor/ARB or sacubitril-valsartan, beta-blocker, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist, and SGLT2 inhibitor, plus device therapy where indicated. Specialist heart failure nurse follow-up every few weeks while titrating, with daily weight monitoring, fluid and salt advice, and cardiac rehabilitation.

name: Alzheimer disease
summary: A progressive neurodegenerative dementia with insidious decline in episodic memory and later language, visuospatial, and executive function, eventually affecting independence.
treatment: Diagnosis in a memory clinic with cognitive testing, blood tests, and brain imaging, then an acetylcholinesterase inhibitor for mild to moderate disease and memantine for moderate to severe disease, with cognitive stimulation and carer support. Regular review of cognition, behaviour, safety, driving, and advance care planning, avoiding antipsychotics where possible.
duration: lifelong and progressive, with periodic review

name: Rheumatoid arthritis
summary: A chronic autoimmune inflammatory arthritis causing symmetrical swelling, pain, and prolonged morning stiffness of the small joints of the hands and feet, leading to joint damage if untreated.
treatment: Early referral to rheumatology and a conventional DMARD (methotrexate first line) started promptly, with short-term corticosteroid bridging, escalating to biologic or targeted synthetic DMARDs if disease activity remains high. Monthly review with blood monitoring (blood count, liver and kidney function) until controlled, then every few months, plus physiotherapy and cardiovascular risk management.

name: Breast cancer (under treatment)
summary: Malignant tumour of breast tissue, usually invasive ductal or lobular carcinoma, managed by a multidisciplinary team according to stage and receptor status (ER, PR, HER2).
treatment: Surgery (breast-conserving surgery or mastectomy with sentinel node biopsy) combined according to stage and receptor status with chemotherapy given in cycles about every 3 weeks, HER2-targeted therapy, radiotherapy, and endocrine therapy for hormone-receptor-positive disease. Bloods and toxicity review before each chemotherapy cycle, then surveillance with clinical review and annual mammography.
duration: months of active treatment, then years of endocrine therapy and surveillance

name: End-stage kidney disease on haemodialysis
summary: Stage 5 chronic kidney disease (eGFR below 15 mL/min/1.73m2) requiring kidney replacement therapy, here in-centre haemodialysis, with fluid, electrolyte, anaemia, and bone-mineral complications.
treatment: In-centre haemodialysis three times a week for about 4 hours through an arteriovenous fistula or catheter, with fluid and potassium restriction, phosphate binders, vitamin D analogues, and erythropoiesis-stimulating agents with iron for anaemia. Monthly bloods and dialysis adequacy review, vascular access surveillance, and transplant assessment where suitable.
